descs: Apple rows climb the combe's slopes on every side, hedge and hive between them.

spots.name: The Hillgap Rows
spots.desc: Where the last apple row gives out, the ground pinches between two hill-shoulders and the old cairn-track climbs north, out of the combe entirely. Wind off the high downs carries iron and cold stone on it.
spots.brief: Rows give out; the cairn-track climbs north.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 5 south and 3 west — and the cairn-track climbs north from this very gap in the hills.

spots.name: Overlook Corner
spots.desc: The highest ground the orchard climbs to, a shoulder of bare rock breaking through the grass. Ash-pale country shows distant east, past more hill than orchard, though no path of yours runs there from this height.
spots.brief: High bare rock; ash country distant east.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 5 south and 4 west. The cairn-track's foot: 1 west.

spots.name: The High Pasture
spots.desc: Sheep-cropped turf above the last apple row, close under the hill's own shoulder. The grass here has never once gone to orchard, too thin and too high for anything but grazing.
spots.brief: Sheep-cropped turf under the hill's shoulder.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 4 south. The cairn-track's foot: 1 north and 3 east.

spots.name: The Beacon Shoulder
spots.desc: The ground rises hard toward a broken tower's foot, steps just visible spiralling up into weather-beaten stone. This is as close as the orchard climbs to the old signal-hill.
spots.brief: Rising ground; a broken tower's foot, up.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 4 south and 1 west. The cairn-track's foot: 1 north and 2 east.

spots.name: Windrow Slope
spots.desc: Apples that rolled clear of their row lie scattered the length of the slope, gone soft where nobody troubled to gather them. A hard wind off the downs strips this row bare before any other.
spots.brief: Windfall apples, scattered and ungathered.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 4 south and 2 west. The cairn-track's foot: 1 north and 1 east.

spots.name: The Sunken Lane
spots.desc: The lane sinks below the orchard's own ground, hedge-banks grown high enough over it to hide a walker from either side. Something has worn a path down its center that isn't cart-wheels.
spots.brief: A sunk, hedge-hidden lane; a worn foot-path.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 4 south and 3 west. The cairn-track's foot: 1 north.

actions.label: read the path for what walks it (wits)
fx: The worn path keeps to the lane's near bank, never the far one, and never past the old hedge-gap. Whatever walks here at night, it keeps to a line as fixed as any patrol's.
The wear looks the same from every angle you try it. It can be read again.

actions.label: read the lane's line at a glance
fx: A worn line reads the same to you as any spoor: near bank, never the far one, never past the hedge-gap. You have the wax-pale guest's walk before you've broken a sweat.

actions.label: cask by the known line (might, 1hp fail)
fx: You keep to the far bank the whole way, and the cask never so much as shifts. Something wax-pale stands at the lane's near end the whole crossing and never once steps toward you.
A root catches your foot mid-lane, and the cask nearly goes with you. It stays dry, barely, and so do you. It can be tried again.

actions.label: carry the cask, blind (might, 2hp fail)
fx: You guess a line through the dark and guess right, cask held high the whole way. Something wax-pale watches from the hedge-gap, cup still in hand, and lets you pass.
You take the near bank without knowing better, and something wax-pale is suddenly very close. You get the cask through anyway, shaking. It can be tried again.

spots.name: The Far Shoulder
spots.desc: The orchard's easternmost high ground, thin soil and thinner trees. From here the ground falls away toward the old burned road, though the way down from this exact spot is nothing but a rumor of a path.
spots.brief: Thin high ground; the burned road distant.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 4 south and 4 west. The cairn-track's foot: 1 north and 1 west.

spots.name: The Waxway
spots.desc: A narrow track worn by hive-keepers' feet runs in along the hill's foot toward a crack in the rock, honey-smell and cold stone air drifting from it in equal measure.
spots.brief: A hive-keepers' track; a cave-mouth, in.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 3 south. The cairn-track's foot: 2 north and 3 east.

spots.name: Middle Row
spots.desc: An ordinary row of ordinary trees, exactly what an orchard row ought to be and nothing more, which after the rest of this combe feels like its own kind of relief.
spots.brief: An ordinary, unremarkable orchard row.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 3 south and 1 west. The cairn-track's foot: 2 north and 2 east.

spots.name: The Fallen Bough
spots.desc: A whole tree lies where it toppled, roots up, apples still ripening along branches that no longer reach any sun worth the name. Nobody has cleared it in years anyone can put a number to.
spots.brief: A fallen tree, apples still ripening on it.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 3 south and 2 west. The cairn-track's foot: 2 north and 1 east.

spots.name: Hedgerow Turn
spots.desc: The orchard rows bend sharply here around an old hedge-line, wax-comb tucked into its thickest tangles. Bees work the turn even on a still day, loud enough to hear before you see them.
spots.brief: A bent hedge-line; bees working it loudly.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 3 south and 3 west. The cairn-track's foot: 2 north.

spots.name: The Grafting Row
spots.desc: Young trees stand grafted onto older rootstock, bark still scarred where the cuts were bound. Someone here still means for this orchard to outlast whatever argument is fought over who owns it.
spots.brief: Young grafted trees on old rootstock.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 3 south and 4 west. The cairn-track's foot: 2 north and 1 west.

spots.name: The Hive Hedge
spots.desc: A long hedge stitched thick with woven skeps, wax and smoke-smell heavy on the air even at a distance. This is where Mootcombe's honey comes from, and by old custom half the hall's candles once did too.
spots.brief: A hedge thick with skeps; heavy wax-smell.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 south and 1 east. The cairn-track's foot: 3 north and 4 east.

spots.name: Cross Row
spots.desc: Two orchard rows meet here at an angle no orchard-keeper would plant on purpose, the seam of some boundary dispute nobody living remembers the terms of.
spots.brief: Two rows crossing at an old boundary's seam.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 south. The cairn-track's foot: 3 north and 3 east.

spots.name: The Long Row
spots.desc: The combe's longest unbroken row runs the whole width of this ground, trees old enough that their trunks have gone the color of the stone beneath them.
spots.brief: The combe's longest unbroken orchard row.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 south and 1 west. The cairn-track's foot: 3 north and 2 east.

spots.name: Chapel Rise
spots.desc: The ground rises toward a low chapel roof, door standing ajar the way it's stood for longer than any lock would have lasted. Kings were shriven here once, before they were crowned under the oak below.
spots.brief: Rising ground; a chapel door standing ajar.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 south and 2 west. The cairn-track's foot: 3 north and 1 east.

spots.name: The Millbrook Ford
spots.desc: The stream that turns the cider-press runs shallow and clear here, easy underfoot even laden. Watercress grows thick along both banks where the current slows.
spots.brief: A shallow, clear stream-crossing.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 south and 3 west. The cairn-track's foot: 3 north.

spots.name: The Last Row
spots.desc: The easternmost row before the orchard gives out to bare verge and, beyond it, the old burned road running on toward ash-country. Fewer trees survive out here than anywhere else in the combe.
spots.brief: The last row; the burned road beyond it.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 south and 4 west. The cairn-track's foot: 3 north and 1 west.

spots.name: The Sheltered Row
spots.desc: Trees stand close in the hill's own lee here, sheltered from every wind that troubles the rest of the combe. Fruit ripens a full week earlier on this row than on any other.
spots.brief: A wind-sheltered row; early-ripening fruit.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 south and 1 east. The cairn-track's foot: 4 north and 4 east.

spots.name: The Drover's Turn
spots.desc: The ground bends where stock used to be driven down toward the ford, worn to a hollow by hooves that stopped coming through generations back. Brambles are winning the argument with the old path.
spots.brief: A worn bend; an old drover's path, brambled.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 south. The cairn-track's foot: 4 north and 3 east.

spots.name: The Moot-Oak's Approach
spots.desc: The last stretch before the moot-green opens out, the moot-oak's own crown visible over the last hedge. Fallen apples lie thicker here than anywhere else, close enough to home that even the birds leave some.
spots.brief: The moot-oak's crown visible over the hedge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 south and 1 west. The cairn-track's foot: 4 north and 2 east.

actions.label: gather a sack of the oak's own apples
fx: You fill a sack from the ground under the oak's own reaching branches. Nobody stops you. Nobody in Mootcombe ever has, until it comes to the pressing.

spots.name: The Cider-Press and Wheel
spots.desc: The press stands under its own lean-to roof, wheel and stream-race both idle. Everything here is sound and ready; it only wants someone willing to turn it, and apples worth the turning.
spots.brief: The idle cider-press; the wheel, unturned.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 south and 2 west. The cairn-track's foot: 4 north and 1 east.

actions.label: turn the wheel (might, 1hp fail)
fx: You put your own back into the wheel, and the press groans awake after four hundred years of standing still. Cider runs thin and gold into the trough — the last course, pressed by a stranger's hand.
The wheel kicks back against you before it gives, and catches your knuckles for the trouble. It can be tried again.

spots.name: Skep Row
spots.desc: Woven skeps stand in ranks along the row's edge, and a low hut sits just past them, smoke curling thin from its chimney regardless of the hour.
spots.brief: Ranked skeps; a low hut just past them.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 south and 3 west. The cairn-track's foot: 4 north.

spots.name: The Bee-Line
spots.desc: Hive-traffic crosses thick over this row in summer, a living road strung between the hedge and the combe's far hives that has nothing to do with any path a person could walk.
spots.brief: Thick hive-traffic crossing overhead.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 south and 4 west. The cairn-track's foot: 4 north and 1 west.

spots.name: The Nether Row
spots.desc: The lowest row in the combe, boggy underfoot where the stream's outflow never quite drains away. Apples here fall early and rot fast, and nobody minds losing this row to it.
spots.brief: The lowest row; boggy, early-falling fruit.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 east. The cairn-track's foot: 5 north and 4 east.

spots.name: Village Rise
spots.desc: The ground rises south toward Mootcombe's own roofs, hearth-smoke visible over the last hedge. This is as close as the orchard proper comes to the village that tends it.
spots.brief: Rising ground; Mootcombe's roofs, south.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe's roofs are right there, south. The cairn-track's foot: 5 north and 3 east.

spots.name: The Wassail Stone
spots.desc: A flat stone stands alone in the grass, worn smooth on top where cups have rested on it longer than anyone living can account for. Cider gets poured over it once a year, feast-day or not.
spots.brief: A flat stone, cup-worn; cider poured yearly.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 1 west. The cairn-track's foot: 5 north and 2 east.

spots.name: Green Row
spots.desc: The row nearest the moot-green, apples here eaten straight off the branch by children more often than they're ever pressed or stored.
spots.brief: The row nearest the green; apples eaten raw.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 2 west. The cairn-track's foot: 5 north and 1 east.

spots.name: The Lower Hedge
spots.desc: A low hedge marks the combe's southern boundary here, more gap than hedge in places where stock has pushed through for generations. Beyond it the ground simply stops being orchard.
spots.brief: A low, gapped hedge; the combe's south edge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 3 west. The cairn-track's foot: 5 north.

spots.name: Combe's End
spots.desc: The last row gives out to plain scrub, the combe's shape finally spent. Nothing beyond here was ever worth an orchard-keeper's trouble to plant.
spots.brief: The last row gives out to scrub.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the combe runs, Mootcombe is 4 west. The cairn-track's foot: 5 north and 1 west.

onEnter: Something moves between the rows behind you, wax-pale and unhurried, a cup held level in one hand as if nothing has spilled from it in four hundred years.

vars.NAME: the Combe Beacon
vars.VIEW: the whole combe spreads below, the moot-oak's crown at its heart and the barred hall's roof north of it, orchard rows on every slope between
vars.SIGN: A rusted beacon-cage hangs at the parapet, unlit longer than anyone has needed calling to a moot.

vars.NAME: the Wax Caves
vars.SIGN: Old wax-seals line the walls in rows — candle-stores once, raided by something with a sweeter tooth than any monk's.
vars.LOOT: a sealed jar of the hall's own candle-wax, unmelted after four hundred years

vars.NAME: the Shriving Chapel
vars.SIGN: The porch step is worn to a bowl-shape, kneeling wearing it long before anything else did.

vars.NAME: the Skep Yard
vars.SIGN: Skeps stand in rows outside, more of them tended than one pair of hands ought to manage alone.
vars.LOOT: a comb of the oak's own honey, dark as the bark it came from

mc_oak_apples.name: a sack of the moot-oak's apples
mc_oak_apples.hint: wants pressing at the wheel, or a hand willing to carry them there

mc_guest.name: a wax-pale guest
mc_guest.desc: Feast-clothes gone the color of old tallow, a cup held level and full in one hand no matter how the rest of him moves.
onDeath: He comes apart into wax and old cloth before he finishes falling, the cup shattering last of all. Somewhere north, for a moment, the barred hall goes entirely silent.
